item.title: He tracked down over 60 poachers and followed a blood trail for 1.5 km: Meet Zorba, the dog who protected Assam’s rhinos
item.description: Zorba, a Belgian Malinois esteemed for his exemplary contributions to wildlife conservation in Assam, was instrumental in tracking more than 60 poachers within Kaziranga National Park. His remarkable ability to retrieve vital evidence and follow scent trails showcased the invaluable role of trained dogs in environmental protection. Honored for his unwavering service, Zorba passed away in November 2022, leaving a lasting impact on both his handlers and the conservation community. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: In 1944, a US Navy serviceman stationed in the Pacific mailed his wife a coconut
item.description: In an extraordinary act of devotion during 1944, U.S. Navy serviceman Raymond sent a carved coconut to his beloved wife, Marie. This unique letter, mailed all the way from Hawaii, bore their names intertwined in a heart, symbolizing their unwavering love. Their enduring marriage of 53 years stands testament to a bond that grew deeper with time. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: A butterfly disappeared from Ontario in 1988 and has not been recorded there since
item.description: In an exciting conservation effort, scientists are set to reintroduce the frosted elfin butterfly to Ontario, a species that vanished nearly forty years ago. Adult butterflies and their eggs are being moved from New York for breeding in captivity before their release. The initial reintroduction is planned for spring 2027 in Port Rowan, where habitats have been carefully restored. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Dr. Amy Acton has been elected as Ohio's first female governor after defeating Vivek Ramaswamy. This historic victory marks the first Democratic win in the state's governorship in two decades. Acton campaigned on healthcare and affordability while highlighting her challenging childhood. item.description: Rideshare company unsuccessfully argued it didn’t employ workers and claimed money paid was not wages under NSW law The rideshare behemoth Uber has suffered a bruising loss in Australia’s high court that will cost it more than $80m in unpaid taxes. The court on Wednesday dismissed Uber’s claim it was not liable to pay payroll tax in New South Wales after it argued that it does not employ drivers and claimed that money paid to its drivers were not wages under state law.
